changes: p1 Vācaspatimiśra: role reduced to 'author'. He wrote the Tattvakaumudī, which is itself a commentary on the Sāṃkhyakārikā, so 'commentator' only repeated the same fact.

p2 Ravinandana: confidence lowered to low. 'ravinaṃdane' could also be a locative meaning 'on the day of the son of Ravi', i.e. Saturday (Śani), but that would contradict 'śukravāsare' (Friday). This alternative is now in the notes.
Place: as_written changed to the compound as it appears ('muḍiṣusthāna-vāstavyaṃ'). It is a residence statement, not an explicit statement of where the copy was made.

notes: The scribe line 'muḍiṣusthānavāstavyaṃ liṣyate(!) ravinaṃdane' is ungrammatical. It means roughly 'written (likhyate) by Ravinandana, resident of Muḍiṣu-sthāna', with the instrumental expected but the locative written. Another reading is possible: 'ravinandane' as a locative meaning 'on the day of Ravi's son (Śani)', i.e. Saturday. That reading leaves no scribe name, and Saturday conflicts with 'śukravāsare' (Friday), so the personal-name reading is kept, with low confidence. Muḍiṣu is not identified. The sentence gives the scribe's residence and only implies the place of copying. ŚS 1707 = c. 1785 CE, which agrees with the catalogue. A Revatī nakṣatra on Āṣāḍha kṛṣṇa 10 is astronomically plausible; the weekday has not been checked. Vācaspati's title 'miśra' has been moved to titles.
